page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-24xl is a storage-optimized bare-metal server powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv9-based AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The architecture features 2 MB of L2 cache per core and 36 MB of L3 cache, paired with 768 GB of DDR5 memory. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 60,000 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core CPU performance, particularly in stress-ng multi-core tests, PassMark database operations, and Redis SET operations, which reached 199.43 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with read-only large block transfers reaching 481.78 GB/sec and write large block transfers at 217.96 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate to strong, as evidenced by Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core metrics.

The ARM64 architecture lacks x86-specific vector extensions like AVX or AMX, and the absence of dedicated GPUs limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, resulting in poor text generation speeds for smaller LLM models. However, the high density of physical cores, DDR5 memory, and massive local NVMe storage provides high qualitative cost efficiency for data-intensive workloads, avoiding the hyperthreading overhead of traditional virtualized instances.

This server is optimized for large-scale relational and non-relational databases, high-throughput Redis caching layers, massive data warehousing, software compilation, and high-velocity static web serving.
